title: GO-and-CCC-analyses
text: following code visualises detected signalling pathway using CellChat’s circle layout.
code: detected_pathways <- unique(unlist(lapply(   ccc_results,   function(x) x$cellchat@netP$pathways )))  if (length(detected_pathways) > 0L) {   pathway <- detected_pathways[1]   for (method in names(ccc_results)) {     cellchat <- ccc_results[[method]]$cellchat     if (!is.null(cellchat) && pathway %in% cellchat@netP$pathways) {       CellChat::netVisual_aggregate(         cellchat,         signaling = pathway,         layout = "circle"       )     }   } }

Development note: vignette currently uses DLPFC SpatialExperiment object stored author’s HPC. suitable testing environment, data-loading step must replaced publicly accessible example vignette can reproduced users built public CI service. analyses (particularly nnSVG, SingleR BANKSY) may take time.

title: Benchmarking normalisation methods with STBench
text: DLPFC use human brain-related gene symbols instead mouse-heart markers original testing script. include markers associated cortical layers, neurons, oligodendrocytes astrocytes. Check dataset row names contain gene symbols; contain Ensembl IDs, identifiers must reconciled plots can interpreted. compare SVG likelihood-ratio statistics rankings across normalisation methods. Smaller SVG ranks indicate higher relative priority.
code: marker_genes <- c(   "MBP", "MOBP", "MAG", "PLP1", "PCP4",   "GFAP", "AQP4", "SLC17A7", "SNAP25",   "GAD1", "GAD2", "OLIG1", "OLIG2" )  # Verify that the selected symbols occur in this dataset. intersect(marker_genes, rownames(svg_norm$scran)) #> [1] "MBP"     "PLP1"    "GFAP"    "SLC17A7" "SNAP25" p_svg_markers <- plot_svg_stat(   svg_norm = svg_norm,   genes = marker_genes,   stat = "LR_stat",   method_order = NULL,   method_colors = NULL,   transform = "log",   point_size = 3,   gene_id = "rownames",   theme_name = "bw" ) p_svg_markers$plot p_svg_rank <- plot_svg_rank(   svg_norm = svg_norm,   genes = marker_genes,   method_order = NULL,   method_colors = NULL,   point_size = 3,   gene_id = "rownames",   theme_name = "bw" ) p_svg_rank$plot

title: Benchmarking normalisation methods with STBench
text: compare housekeeping-gene SVG statistics exploratory diagnostic. genes guaranteed spatially uniform; behaviour interpreted context tissue.  also calculate proportion selected housekeeping genes among top 50, 100, 200 300 ranked SVGs.
code: housekeeping_genes <- c(   "GAPDH", "ACTB", "HPRT1", "B2M", "PPIA",   "RPL13A", "RPLP0", "TBP", "GUSB" ) p_svg_hk <- plot_svg_gene_set_distribution(   svg_norm = svg_norm,   genes = housekeeping_genes,   stat = "LR_stat",   method_order = NULL,   method_colors = NULL,   gene_id = "rownames",   transform = "log",   plot_type = "boxplot",   add_jitter = TRUE,   point_size = 1.5,   alpha = 1,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_svg_hk$plot p_svg_topn <- plot_svg_topn_gene_set(   svg_norm = svg_norm,   genes = housekeeping_genes,   top_n = c(50, 100, 200, 300),   method_order = NULL,   method_colors = NULL,   gene_id = "rownames",   theme_name = "classic" ) p_svg_topn$plot

title: Benchmarking normalisation methods with STBench
text: compare distribution SVG statistics biological markers housekeeping genes. transformed statistics displayed separately gene set.
code: gene_sets <- list(   "Housekeeping genes" = housekeeping_genes,   "Biological markers" = marker_genes )  p_svg_sets <- plot_svg_gene_sets(   svg_norm = svg_norm,   gene_sets = gene_sets,   stat = "LR_stat",   method_order = NULL,   method_colors = NULL,   gene_id = "rownames",   transform = "log",   plot_type = "boxplot",   scales = "free_y",   facet_ncol = 3,   add_jitter = TRUE,   point_size = 1,   alpha = 0.65,   jitter_alpha = 0.5,   box_width = 0.65,   title = "Spatial variability across gene sets",   subtitle = NULL,   x_label = "Normalisation method",   y_label = "Log likelihood-ratio statistic",   show_legend = FALSE,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_svg_sets$plot

title: Benchmarking normalisation methods with STBench
text: visualise selected DLPFC markers across normalisation methods. scaled plot, expression rescaled interval 0 1 gene across selected methods. can also plot unscaled assay values; numerical scales may directly comparable methods return different kinds transformed expression.
code: spatial_markers <- c(   "MBP", "MOBP", "PCP4", "GFAP", "SLC17A7", "GAD1" )  p_marker_maps <- plot_spatial_expression(   norm_list = norm,   genes = c("MBP", "MOBP", "PCP4", "GFAP"),   methods = c("None", "scran", "SpaNorm"),   assay_name = "logcounts",   method_order = NULL,   scale_expr = TRUE,   scale_by = "gene",   point_size = 0.5,   colour_option = "magma",   ncol_genes = 1,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_marker_maps$plot p_spatial_unscaled <- plot_spatial_expression(   norm_list = norm,   genes = spatial_markers,   assay_name = "logcounts",   method_order = NULL,   scale_expr = FALSE,   point_size = 0.5,   colour_option = "magma",   ncol_genes = 1,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_spatial_unscaled$plot

title: Getting started with STBench
text: STBench R package comparing normalisation methods spatial transcriptomics.

title: Getting started with STBench
code: data(spe_example) data(norm_example)  dim(spe_example) #> NULL names(norm_example) #> [1] "None"    "SpaNorm"

title: Getting started with STBench
text: first calculate spot-level metrics, including library size, detected genes mitochondrial fraction, together gene-level expression summaries. inspect distributions filtering.
code: spe <- add_qcs(   spe_example,   assay_name = "counts",   mito_pattern = "^mt-|^MT-" )  p_qc <- plot_qc(   spe,   bins = 45,   show_density = TRUE,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_qc$plot

title: Getting started with STBench
text: examine relationship possible cutoffs proportions spots genes removed, without performing filtering. use illustrative rather dataset-specific thresholds.
code: p_cutoffs <- plot_qc_cutoffs(   spe,   library_cutoff = 6.5,   gene_cutoff = 0.2,   n_points = 100,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_cutoffs$plot

title: Getting started with STBench
text: remove spots genes selected thresholds. Choose cutoffs appropriate dataset.
code: spe_filtered <- filter_qc(   spe,   library_cutoff = 2.5,   gene_cutoff = 0.2,   recalculate = TRUE,   assay_name = "counts",   mito_pattern = "^mt-|^MT-" ) plot_qc(spe_filtered, theme_name = "classic")$plot

title: Getting started with STBench
text: None method provides log1p-transformed baseline. Method-specific arguments supplied params. execute normalisation small dataset; subsequent comparisons, use saved norm_example consistent reference.
code: norm_recomputed <- normalize_spe(   spe_example,   methods = c("None", "SpaNorm"),   params = list(     spanorm = list(       sample_p = 0.15,       df_tps = 6,       adj_method = "logpac",       seed = 123     )   ) ) norm <- norm_example lapply(norm, dim) #> $None #> [1]  50 944 #>  #> $SpaNorm #> [1]  50 944

title: Getting started with STBench
text: compare summed normalised expression across spots. comparison uses normalisation methods example dataset.
code: p_ls <- plot_library_size_comparison(   norm,   methods = names(norm),   assay_name = "logcounts",   point_size = 0.5,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_ls$plot

title: Getting started with STBench
text: run PCA UMAP independently normalisation method colour available cell-type annotation.
code: umap_data <- get_umap_data(   norm,   methods = names(norm),   prop_spots = 1,   seed = 123,   assay_name = "logcounts",   n_pcs = 10,   n_neighbors = 15 ) p_umap <- plot_umap_comparison(   umap_data,   colour_by = "cell_type",   point_size = 1,   alpha = 0.6,   ncol = 2,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_umap$plot

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
text: use SVG detection procedure normalised dataset examine normalisation affects spatial variability statistics gene rankings. supplied svg_example contains precomputed results, avoiding repeated, potentially expensive nnSVG calculations.
code: data(norm_example) data(svg_example) norm <- norm_example svg_norm <- svg_example names(svg_norm) #> [1] "None"    "SpaNorm"

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
text: reproduce SVG detection normalised data, run code . remaining sections use supplied precomputed results.
code: svg_recomputed <- run_svg(   norm_list = norm,   method = "nnSVG",   n_threads = 1,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
text: evaluate example genes available SVG results rather assuming particular tissue-marker panel present small dataset.
code: common_genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(svg_norm, rownames)) marker_genes <- head(common_genes, 5) marker_genes #> [1] "HSPB7"   "KCNC3"   "COL25A1" "MAL"     "CPXM2"

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
text: Higher likelihood-ratio (LR) statistics indicate stronger statistical evidence spatial variation.
code: if (length(marker_genes) > 0L) {   p_svg_markers <- plot_svg_stat(     svg_norm = svg_norm,     genes = marker_genes,     stat = "LR_stat",     transform = "log",     point_size = 4,     gene_id = "rownames",     theme_name = "bw"   )   p_svg_markers$plot }

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
text: Smaller ranks indicate higher relative priority SVG detection.
code: if (length(marker_genes) > 0L) {   p_svg_rank <- plot_svg_rank(     svg_norm = svg_norm,     genes = marker_genes,     point_size = 3,     gene_id = "rownames",     theme_name = "bw"   )   p_svg_rank$plot }

what: Investigate SVG ranks against LR statistics
title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
code: if (length(marker_genes) > 0L) {   p <- plot_svg_rank_vs_stat(     svg_norm = svg_norm,     genes = marker_genes,     stat = "LR_stat",     transform = "log",     scales = "free",     ncol = 3,     point_size = 3,     theme_name = "bw"   )   p$plot }

what: Compare overall marker gene SVG statistics
title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
code: if (length(marker_genes) > 0L) {   p_svg_mk <- plot_svg_gene_set_distribution(     svg_norm = svg_norm,     genes = marker_genes,     stat = "LR_stat",     gene_id = "rownames",     transform = "log",     plot_type = "boxplot",     add_jitter = TRUE,     point_size = 1.5,     theme_name = "bw"   )   p_svg_mk$plot }

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
text: Correlations calculated using genes shared across methods. Higher correlations indicate greater similarity rankings.
code: p_cor <- plot_svg_rank_correlation(   svg_norm = svg_norm,   show_values = TRUE,   digits = 2,   theme_name = "classic" ) p_cor$plot

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
text: Housekeeping genes generally expected exhibit relatively stable expression, although necessarily spatially uniform. tissue-specific, curated list preferable full analyses. self-contained demonstration, use small subset available genes illustrative gene set. genes claimed housekeeping genes.
code: example_gene_set <- head(common_genes, 10) if (length(example_gene_set) > 0L) {   p_svg_set <- plot_svg_gene_set_distribution(     svg_norm = svg_norm,     genes = example_gene_set,     stat = "LR_stat",     gene_id = "rownames",     transform = "log",     plot_type = "boxplot",     add_jitter = TRUE,     point_size = 1.5,     theme_name = "classic"   )   p_svg_set$plot }

title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
code: if (length(example_gene_set) > 0L) {   p_topn <- plot_svg_topn_gene_set(     svg_norm = svg_norm,     genes = example_gene_set,     top_n = c(10, 20, 50),     gene_id = "rownames",     theme_name = "bw",     gene_set_name = "Example gene set"   )   p_topn$plot }

what: Compare SVG statistics between gene sets
title: Spatially variable gene analysis with STBench
